penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: A $5–15 one-time browser extension requires hundreds to thousands of paying individual consumers to generate meaningful revenue; the model fundamentally needs B2C scale.

penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Building, publishing, and maintaining a browser extension requires real software development (JavaScript, Chrome/Firefox manifest, store submissions, security reviews) that the factory cannot deliver via Claude prompts alone.

rationale: The pain is real and frequent for a narrow set of power users, and CleanShot X's success shows willingness to pay exists in the broader screenshot category. However, the buyer is an individual consumer (not a business buyer), the product requires actual browser extension development that this factory cannot build, distribution via browser extension stores is competitive and slow, and the $5–15 one-time price point demands consumer scale. Total after penalties is 1.3 — well below threshold.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using this factory. A browser extension requires JavaScript development, Chrome Web Store/Firefox Add-ons submission and review (which involves human identity verification, policy compliance, and iterative rejection cycles), and ongoing maintenance for each browser version update. Claude cannot write and ship a browser extension end-to-end without a developer. Additionally, the revenue model ($5–15 one-time, B2C) would require thousands of customers for meaningful income. Recommend dropping entirely.
notes: Failing build gates: buildability_with_ai (2 < 6 required), buyer_clarity (4 < 6 required), operational_autonomy (5 < 7 required). Browser extension development is outside the factory's tooling scope.
